title: Shimon bar Narshiya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, chapter 3, at the end of halakhah 1, Hyman cites “Rabbi Abba bar Kahana, Shimon bar Narshiya, in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.” He cites the statement under the name Shimon Narshiya at the end of halakhah 4. Hyman thinks the name probably refers to a place.

notes.text: The source does not state the link between Abba bar Kahana and Shimon explicitly. The second form is Shimon Garshiya, without an added bar. The place-name explanation is tentative.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Kilayim3:1 scalar has Abba bar Kahana and Shimon bar Narshiya in full Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish’s name;3:4 has Shimon Narshiya without bar. Hyman’s second form is Garshiya, which remains alongside that named Narshiya difference. The unconnected chain is preserved without inventing a reporting verb. Hyman considers a place-name explanation likely; it is neither an identified location nor canonical identity.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1206) reads Narshiya in both passages. The supplied transcription has Garshiya in the second. The Guggenheimer Hebrew at Kilayim 3:1:5 and 3:4:6 reads Narshiya and has bar only in the first passage. The first link in the chain has no explicit reporting verb. Guggenheimer translates the name as “from Nerash” and notes that the Rome manuscript omits bar in the first passage.
